title: How Does Tap to Pay Actually Work?
sources: Wikipedia / NFC Forum, 'Near-field communication': NFC works at 13.56 MHz over a range of about 4 cm or less; the reader (initiator) makes a radio-frequency field that can power a passive target, so passive tags and cards need no battery (inductive coupling between loop antennas)

Wikipedia, 'Contactless payment' and EMV contactless specification: contactless EMV cards contain a chip and a loop antenna around the card; each transaction produces a unique cryptogram, so captured data cannot be replayed for another purchase

Apple Support, 'Apple Pay security and privacy overview' (support.apple.com/en-us/101554): when you add a card, a unique Device Account Number is created and stored instead of your card number; payments use this number plus a transaction-specific dynamic security code, and your actual card number is not stored on the device or shared with merchants
Mastercard, 'What is tokenization' (2025): tokenization replaces the card number with a unique digital identifier (token) so the real card details are not shared during payment

lines.text: How does your card pay just by tapping?
lines.caps: HOW DOES YOUR *CARD | PAY JUST BY *TAPPING?

lines.text: Well, inside the plastic hides a tiny chip and a coil of wire,
lines.caps: WELL, *INSIDE | THE *PLASTIC | HIDES A TINY *CHIP | AND A *COIL | OF *WIRE

lines.text: The reader sends out a magnetic field,
and once your card gets about four centimetres away,
that field wakes the chip up, just like a wireless charger.
lines.caps: THAT *FIELD | *WAKES | THE CHIP *UP | JUST LIKE A *WIRELESS | *CHARGER

lines.text: The chip then answers by radio, called N F C,
with a one-time code made just for this purchase,
so a copied code is useless.
And your phone goes even further.
It doesn't send your real card number at all, just a stand-in.
lines.caps: IT *DOESN'T | SEND YOUR *REAL | CARD *NUMBER | AT *ALL | JUST A *STAND-IN

lines.text: So the shop gets paid without ever seeing your card.
